ddl:
CREATE TABLE Publication (
    Author VARCHAR(255),
    Price FLOAT,
    Publication_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    Type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255),
    Registration_Status VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Administrator (
    Administrator_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Order (
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Order_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Order_Time DATETIME,
    Payment_Method VARCHAR(255),
    Publication_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Shipping_Address VARCHAR(255),
    PRIMARY KEY (Customer_ID, Publication_ID, Order_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Publication_ID) REFERENCES Publication(Publication_ID)
);
gold_question: A publishing house plans to develop an online store, ACShop, for selling academic publications. The functional requirements are as follows: The online academic publications include papers, academic reports, and lecture materials. Publication information includes Publication ID, Title, Author, Price, and Type. Customer information includes Customer ID, Name, Phone, Email, Password, and Registration Status. ACShop will automatically generate orders, with order information including Publication ID, Customer ID, Shipping Address, Payment Method, Order Status, and Order Time. Administrators are responsible for maintaining the online publication catalog, including adding new publications or updating information on available publications. Administrator information includes Administrator ID, Name, Phone, Email, and Password.
nl_text: The rschema_0473 database contains four tables: Publication, Customer, Administrator, and Order. The Publication table contains information about books, including the author, price, publication ID, title, and type. The Customer table contains information about customers, including their customer ID, email, name, password, phone number, and registration status. The Administrator table contains information about administrators, including their administrator ID, email, name, password, and phone number. The Order table contains information about orders, including the customer ID, order status, order time, payment method, publication ID, shipping address, and primary key (customer ID, publication ID, order time). The Order table also contains foreign keys referencing the Customer and Publication tables.
